rows.subtype: One sweet now, not two later [Actor]
rows.description: A young child cannot wait for a bigger treat and grabs the smaller one at once. The future is hard to picture and the present is loud.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child takes ten rupees today over twenty tomorrow. He may choose patience if the wait is far away but breaks when the reward is near.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager prefers an hour of gaming now over a better grade in months. Distant benefits feel weak while immediate pleasure feels vivid.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student spends his stipend at once, knowing he will want the savings later. He plans to be disciplined next month, and next month repeats the choice.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A wise saver sets up automatic transfers, removes temptations, and makes future rewards concrete so that her present self helps her future self.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A toddler screams for the biscuit at this moment and cannot be comforted by a promise for later. The present is the only time that feels real.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A preschooler can wait a little for a treat when distracted by a game or a song, though he struggles when staring at it. Waiting skills grow with practice and support.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager promises to study tomorrow and scrolls tonight, sure his future self will feel more like working. Tomorrow is always the better time to be disciplined.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 23–26

rows.description: A young professional makes small commitments with a friend or a schedule, and rewards herself now for actions that help later, so that good habits survive the pull of the moment.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17

rows.description: A child after a long school day picks the easiest option or refuses to choose, and melts down over small decisions in the evening.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
